studies.label: Controlled crossover experiment: public transport and university-space ideation

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 16, Section 7, Limitations and Further Research; see also PDF p. 4, Section 4.1
counts_source.quote: The results of this research primarily derive from a cohort of 51 engineering students specializing in Industrial Design and Product Development.

arms.name: ChatGPT-assisted ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation using ChatGPT on university-supplied computers; access to other websites and tools was restricted. Group B receives this condition for the public-transport task and Group A for the university-spaces task. These labels refer to current assistance conditions, not independent parallel groups across both tasks (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

arms.name: Unaided ideation
arms.description: Supervised ideation in a computer-free classroom without external support tools. Group A receives this condition first and Group B receives it after its earlier ChatGPT-assisted task (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 1).

studies.country: Spain (study institution; PDF p. 1 affiliations and PDF p. 4, Section 4.1). Participant nationality is not stated.
studies.task: Third-year industrial design and product development engineering students generated innovative ideas to improve public transport and university spaces, each as a sketch and brief description, with eight unique ideas requested within 30 minutes per task (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1: Students had access to the GPT‐3.5 version of ChatGPT. The model release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or registration reference is stated in the complete paper.

studies.shared_sample: Possible shared sample with c031, Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education (DOI 10.1016/j.tsc.2025.101958), as flagged in forms/c201.json sample_overlap. Matching cohort, design and idea counts suggest overlap, but participant identity is unconfirmed. No c031 statistics are used here.

notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10. Read the complete markdown conversion through the final references, including the full continued qualitative table; no appendix or supplement is present. Every cited PDF page was text-extracted with PyMuPDF. Figures 1 and 7 were also rendered and inspected in memory. PDF and printed page numbers agree. All eight screening-form outcomes are retained for each full-sample task contrast and the combined-task contrast. There are no estimates present in only one extraction and no additional eligible outcome or contrast was found. The supplied diff repeats each task-specific n_total disagreement; each distinct slug-and-field difference has one resolution. A full audit also identified differences in stats.test omitted by the supplied diff and reconciled combined-versus-total slug aliases. Equivalent descriptive and provenance wording was consolidated against the paper. Agreement was independently checked for participant and output counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai and within_person. The participant cohort is explicitly linked to the results in Section 7, but randomized, task-specific and per-condition participant analysis counts are not separately printed. The randomized unit is individual assistance order in a supervised classroom experiment, not intact classrooms. First-task records use first_round, second-task between-sequence records use null, and the combined repeated-person records use paired to flag the crossover design. The paired flag does not claim a paired estimator: participant pairing, clustering and carryover adjustment are unreported. All retained outcomes are with_ai and immediate: the AI condition had ChatGPT available while producing the ideas, and the later evaluation session did not produce new creative outputs. The second-task unaided comparator follows experimental AI exposure, but this is not a separately identified after_ai comparison. Creativity measures overall creativity; Innovation measures novelty; Viability, User benefits, Value and the Is a good idea assessment measure usefulness. Complexity is other, with higher values indicating more complexity rather than a known improvement in creativity. Aggregate idea quantity is fluency with higher_is more_ideas. Peer-rated outcomes use output as the observed unit; printed idea-corpus counts are retained as n_units and are not participant counts or independently verified complete-case counts. The peer raters are students, not the experts who reviewed the instrument. Figure 7 prints no numerical randomized arm means, dispersions, test results or effects. All such statistics remain null, and the undefined error bars leave se_basis unclear. Table 3 supplies only aggregate idea totals, retained in fluency notes and their source quotes; they are not entered as means or used to infer participant counts. Each nonrandom prior-experience comparison, self-report outcome and qualitative reflection is listed in not_extracted. Table 4 statistics are not imported into randomized comparisons. There is no scored diversity outcome or isolated after_ai effect. Possible overlap with c031 remains unconfirmed as flagged in the screening form; no c031 results or participant counts are substituted. No numerical effect, dispersion, count, p-value bound or uncertainty measure was derived, and no figure was digitized.
